cards.text: The word of the LORD comes again to Ezekiel, a priest living in the land of the Chaldeans (Ezekiel 1:3). God calls him "Son of man" and tells him about two women, daughters of the same mother. Fair warning, friend: this one is a heavy picture, so stay close.

cards.question: From their youth, these two sisters were already prostituting themselves. Where did it start?

cards.text: The older sister is named Oholah, and her sister is named Oholibah. Say that three times fast, friend. I tried, and my mustache tied itself in a KNOT.

cards.question: God says both sisters became His, and they stand for two cities. Which city is Oholah, the older sister?
Oholibah, her sister, stands for the city of ___.

cards.text: Oholah goes first. She starts chasing other lovers.

cards.question: Oholah only chased other lovers after she stopped belonging to God.

cards.text: Her lovers are warriors clothed in blue, governors and commanders, desirable young men on horseback. I bet those uniforms did a LOT of the talking.

cards.question: Who are these warriors in blue that Oholah chases?
Oholah gives herself to all the elite of Assyria, and she defiles herself with all their ___.

cards.text: None of this is new, friend. She never gave up what she started in Egypt in her youth, so God steps in.

cards.question: God steps in against Oholah. Into whose hands does He deliver her?
Oholah's lovers protect her sons and daughters.

cards.text: Instead, they expose her, seize her children and put her to the sword. Her name becomes a byword among women, and there's still one more sister in this story.
Oholibah saw everything that happened to her sister.

cards.question: After seeing what happened to Oholah, what does Oholibah do?

answers.text: She turns back to God for good
She grieves and stays away from lovers

cards.text: That's like watching your sister grab a hot cookie sheet bare-handed, then grabbing it with BOTH hands. And Oholibah starts chasing lovers of her own.

cards.question: Oholibah chases the same Assyrians her sister chased.

cards.text: God says both sisters took the same path. But Oholibah goes further: she sees men engraved on a wall in vermilion, with belts on their waists and flowing turbans on their heads.

cards.question: The men engraved on the wall look like officers of which people?

cards.text: She hasn't even MET these men. She's going off pictures on a wall, and friend, that's like falling for a cookie because of the photo on the box.

cards.question: At the sight of them, Oholibah lusts for them and sends ___ to them in Chaldea.

cards.text: So the Babylonians come to her, and they defile her.

cards.question: Once the Babylonians have defiled her, how does Oholibah feel about them?

answers.text: She wants to marry their king

cards.question: When Oholibah openly prostitutes herself, God turns away from her just as He did from her sister.

cards.text: Then Oholibah's mind goes back to the days of her youth.

cards.question: Oholibah remembers how she prostituted herself in her youth, in the land of ___.
Remembering her youth makes Oholibah turn back from her ways.

cards.text: She goes back to the lovers of her youth. Then God speaks right to her: "So you revisited the indecency of your youth…"
Now the Lord GOD speaks straight to Oholibah. The lovers she chased are about to be turned against her.

cards.question: God says He'll stir up Oholibah's lovers against her. Which ones?

answers.text: The ones she turned from in disgust
The ones she never got to meet
The ones who still love her deeply

cards.text: The list is long: the Babylonians, all the Chaldeans, the men of Pekod, Shoa and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them. All of them showing up together is like every oven timer in my bakery going off at the SAME TIME.

cards.question: Oholibah's lovers will come against her from only one side.

cards.text: They bring weapons, chariots and wagons, with bucklers, shields and helmets. And God says He'll hand judgment over to them.

cards.question: God hands judgment over to Oholibah's lovers. By whose standards will they punish her?

cards.text: God says He'll set His jealous rage against her, and they'll deal with her in fury. They'll cut off noses and ears, and survivors will fall by the sword.

cards.question: Just like her sister, Oholibah will have her sons and daughters seized.

cards.text: They'll strip off her clothes and take her fine jewelry.

cards.question: Through all of this, what does God say He will put an end to?
God says Oholibah won't lift her eyes to them or remember ___ anymore.

cards.text: God says it again: He'll deliver her into the hands of those she hates. They'll take all she worked for and leave her naked and bare.

cards.question: God gives the reason. What brought all of this on Oholibah?

answers.text: Chasing the nations and their idols
A famine sent on her fields

cards.text: Because she followed her sister's path, God says He'll put something of her sister's in her hand.

cards.question: Because she followed her sister's path, God will put her sister's ___ in her hand.

cards.text: It's a cup deep and wide, and it will bring scorn and derision, for it holds so much. It's a cup of devastation and desolation, the cup of her sister Samaria.

cards.question: Oholibah will only take a small sip from her sister's cup.
At the end, the Lord GOD names the root of it all. What is it?

answers.text: She forgot Him and cast Him behind her back
She trusted her sister more than Him
She never once heard His word spoken

cards.text: Whew. I need a minute after that one, friend, and this word about the two sisters isn't finished yet.

findings.problem: Half of the stop's choice cards are pure discovery questions that can't be reasoned out from the earlier cards. These are card 2 (where it started: Egypt), card 4 (Oholah is Samaria), card 5 (Oholibah is Jerusalem) and card 9 (the warriors in blue are the Assyrians). The story cards before them give no clues, so a baker who doesn't already know the answers is guessing.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The card ends with 'so God steps in', which is verse 9 ('Therefore I delivered her'), but it cites only Ezekiel 23:8. The 'so' also ties God's action to verse 8 alone, when verse 9's 'Therefore' follows all of verses 5 to 8.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: 'Oholibah starts chasing lovers of her own' suggests she chases different lovers. Verse 12 says 'She too lusted after the Assyrians', the same lovers her sister chased. The line also steers the baker toward the wrong answer on card 4's true or false.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The card tells about the belts on their waists and the flowing turbans on their heads, which come from verse 15, but it cites only Ezekiel 23:13-14.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This card asks again that the sisters' youthful prostitution took place in Egypt. That was already asked in stop 1, card 2 (verse 3) and told again in stop 1, card 11 (verse 8). Verse 19 repeats the same line, so it shouldn't be asked a second time.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: 'She goes back to the lovers of her youth' isn't what the text says. In verse 20, lusting after the Egyptian lovers is part of what she remembers from her youth. Verse 21 says she 'revisited the indecency of your youth', not that she went back to those lovers.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Her sister's standards' doesn't make sense as a standard of punishment. Oholah has already been judged and put to the sword, so the answer reads as filler rather than a believable choice.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: In 'won't lift her eyes to them', the word 'them' points to no one the baker can see on the card. In the text it refers back to the indecency that began in Egypt.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'She forgot Him and cast Him behind her back', uses the Bible's own idiom and is longer than the wrong answers. It sounds more like Scripture than 'She trusted her sister more than Him' and 'She never once heard His word spoken', so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: This last story card is only the line saying the word isn't finished, which the docs allow when the last verse is asked on a choice card. It tells no verse, but it cites Ezekiel 23:35.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verse, what should its 'verses' field cite? Should it repeat the last verse, or use some other value?
